name: linkat
synopsis: int linkat(int olddirfd, const char *oldpath, int newdirfd, const char *newpath, int flags);
description: The linkat() system call creates a new hard link to an existing file, similar to link(), but allows specifying directories via file descriptors and additional flags. It interprets paths relative to the provided directory file descriptors.

parameters.name: olddirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for oldpath, or AT_FDCWD for current working directory

parameters.name: oldpath
parameters.description: Pathname of the existing file to link

parameters.name: newdirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for newpath, or AT_FDCWD for current working directory

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control behavior, such as AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW or AT_EMPTY_PATH

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Write access to the directory containing newpath is denied, or search permission is denied for one of the directories in the path prefix of oldpath or newpath
The user’s quota of disk blocks on the filesystem has been exhausted
oldpath or newpath points outside your accessible address space
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving oldpath or newpath
The file referred to by oldpath already has the maximum number of links to it
oldpath or newpath was too long
A directory component in oldpath or newpath does not exist or is a dangling symbolic link
The device containing the file has no room for the new directory entry
A component used as a directory in oldpath or newpath is not, in fact, a directory
oldpath is a directory, or the filesystem does not support hard links, or other permission issues
The file is on a read-only filesystem
oldpath and newpath are not on the same mounted filesystem
oldpath or newpath is relative but the corresponding dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor
An invalid flag value was specified in flags
AT_EMPTY_PATH was specified but the caller lacks CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, or other path-related issues

bugs: On NFS filesystems, the return code may be wrong if the NFS server performs the link creation and dies before confirming it; use stat(2) to verify if the link was created.
